Q: How do quantization and low-rank adaptation affect quality, memory and release compatibility?
A:
Quantization changes numerical representation and can reduce parameter storage or computation under supported kernels. Low-rank adaptation learns constrained updates to selected layers while retaining a base model. Neither guarantees faster end-to-end inference on every device or unchanged quality.

Account for activation and cache memory, loading overhead and actual target hardware. Version the base model, tokenizer, adapter and quantization profile together, then evaluate important slices and reject incompatible combinations. A small mechanism exercise is not evidence of production-scale adaptation quality.
Why: An adapter trained for one base revision may load structurally against another but change behavior unexpectedly. Require a compatible base identity and evaluate the assembled model rather than treating matching tensor shapes as sufficient.
Risk: Parameter compression can leave attention-cache memory or latency as the dominant bottleneck.
Trade: Measure the complete target workload before choosing a compression or adaptation method.
Try: Compare compatible and incompatible model manifests and state the unmeasured hardware limits.
